html:
The Great Syrian Revolt was an uprising against French rule in Syria from 1925 to 1927. It began among the Druze of the Jabal al-Druze, led by Sultan al-Atrash, and spread to Damascus and other regions.

France held Syria under a mandate of the League of Nations after the First World War (French Mandate for Syria and Lebanon). It had split the country into separate states and ruled through harsh officers. In 1925 the Druze rebels beat French columns, and nationalists in the cities joined them.

In October 1925 French artillery and planes shelled Damascus for two days, killing many civilians and causing an outcry in Europe. The revolt was crushed by 1927. It made Sultan al-Atrash a national hero and pushed France toward talks that led to independence in 1946.
sum: The Great Syrian Revolt was an uprising against French rule in Syria from 1925 to 1927. It began among the Druze of the Jabal al-Druze, led by Sultan al-Atrash, and spread to Damascus and other regions.
